approach: Split the work into a pure measurement, a pure trigger and one model call. (1) status.rs gets `Throughput::compute(&Records)`, which reads only job records. Per landed job it takes stage minutes from Reader (reading), Planner+Critic (planning), Producer, Verifier invocations (ended_at minus started_at), from verification.checks[].duration (checks), and from the tail between the last invocation's end and the landing outcome time (landing and rebuild, one stage because no record separates a rebuild). It reports landed per UTC day, median total and per-stage minutes over the newest THROUGHPUT_WINDOW=20 landed jobs, idle time (gaps between merged job intervals), and minutes spent on closed non-landed jobs and plan-stopped jobs. It is a `StatusView.throughput` field with a `text()` method, printed by display.rs like `check_durations`. (2) records.rs gets one new kind, `athena.throughput-review/1`, at `records/throughput-reviews/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json`, modelled on CodeHealthBaseline. It holds landings, window median, trigger, an optional proposal (bottleneck, change, expected_minutes_saved, priority, request_job) and `followups` (predicted vs measured). `Records` gains `throughput_reviews`. (3) hestia.rs gets pure `throughput_due` (first review at 10 landed jobs; then 10 more landings since the last review, or window median more than 1.2 times the last review's median with at least one new landing), pure `priority_for_minutes`, pure `throughput_followups`, a request builder going through `StewardRequest::new`, and `Athena::throughput_review(ui)`. That method is called from `review_passes`. It writes the section and a copy of docs/design into a scratch workspace, asks the model through agent_spec/invoke_and_record (Role::Steward, `models.verifier`, as steward, auditor and audience already do), validates the JSON, queues one design request unless an open one carries the marker, and commits the review record and invocation in one records commit. A model failure still commits a review record with no proposal, so cadence advances and a broken model is not retried on every drain. (4) code_health.rs: `REVIEW_EVERY` is reused as the throughput cadence and its doc comment names that; there is no logic change and no change to design-review behavior. (5) docs/design/hestia.md and CHANGELOG.md get the cadence, prediction and follow-up text.

decisions.choice: Compute throughput purely from Records (job records), with no git history.
decisions.reason: Records hold invocation started_at/ended_at, verification check durations and outcome.at, so status and the review share one number, and tests build Records in memory or commit them with the existing `put` helper. The trigger and the status median use the same THROUGHPUT_WINDOW.

rejected.option: Count landings from git first-parent history like code_health::landings.
rejected.why: Needs a git fixture per test and can disagree with the records-based median it is compared against.
Gives no per-stage split and omits reading, planning and landing.

decisions.choice: Fold landing and rebuild into one stage: outcome.at (later_outcome first) minus the end of the job's last invocation, floored at 0.
decisions.reason: No record separates the post-landing rebuild, which happens in the drain after landing (drain.rs Steps::rebuild). The brief asks for 'landing and rebuild'. The doc and the text() label say what is measured.

rejected.why: Out of scope; it would widen the change into drain.rs and the records schema for jobs.

decisions.choice: New record kind athena.throughput-review/1, modelled on CodeHealthBaseline, holding the cadence state, the prediction and the follow-ups.
decisions.reason: The cadence needs a durable last-review point (landings, median). The prediction must outlive the request. Records is the system of record, and the kind needs a path, an AnyRecord variant, check_record_file acceptance and a round-trip test.

rejected.why: It has no median, prediction or follow-up fields, and the design review must not change.

rejected.option: Keep the prediction only in the request text.
rejected.why: The measured follow-up would parse prose, and a closed request would lose it.

decisions.choice: A cited change is a landed request job, other than the design request itself, whose text contains the review's record id. The design request body tells the author to cite that id. Measured minutes are the window median of landed jobs whose outcome.at is later than the cited job's landing, capped at the newest 10 and needing at least 1. The record keeps baseline (the review's median), predicted saving, measured median and measured saving. A follow-up is written once per review.
decisions.reason: Deterministic and testable from records. The design request lands a note and not the speedup, so it is excluded.

rejected.option: Treat the design request's own landing as the cited change.
rejected.why: It lands a design note, which changes no pipeline timing.

decisions.choice: Priority from expected minutes saved: 10 or more is urgent, 5 or more is high, 2 or more is normal, below 2 is low (named consts, pure `priority_for_minutes`). Passed to `StewardRequest::new`.
decisions.reason: Speed first (OP-23): a larger saving gets a higher priority, and the mapping is monotonic and unit-testable.

rejected.option: Always urgent, as the root-cause request is.
rejected.why: The brief says priority is set by expected minutes saved.

decisions.choice: Duplicate suppression: a non-Closed request job with a line starting with the marker 'Throughput design: ' means no new request is queued. The review still writes its record, with the proposal's request_job empty and a note.
decisions.reason: Matches structural_pass_open. It does not depend on the review record having committed, so a crash between queue and commit cannot make a duplicate.

rejected.option: Skip the whole review while a request is open.
rejected.why: The cadence would stall and a follow-up could not be recorded.

decisions.choice: Call `throughput_review` from `review_passes`, adding a third summary line. It never fails the caller.
decisions.reason: review_passes is the existing housekeeping run at drain start and in sweeps. The trigger is a pure check, so a normal drain makes no model call.

rejected.why: Puts a strong-model wait inside the landing path that the review exists to shorten.

decisions.choice: Use Role::Steward and `models.verifier`, the existing borrowed-model pattern, with no new Role and no config change.
decisions.reason: A new Role would ripple through Role::as_str, budgets and the records match arms. athena.toml and defaults.toml are out of scope.

Run cargo test -p athena-data records.

status.rs: implement `Throughput::compute(&Records)` over request jobs. Stage minutes: sum of (ended_at - started_at) for Reader, for Planner+Critic, for Producer and for Verifier invocations; checks from verification.checks durations (skip `not run` as test_check_seconds does); landing/rebuild is the outcome.at (later_outcome first) minus the last invocation end, floored at 0. Median over the newest THROUGHPUT_WINDOW landed jobs by landing time. Landed per UTC date over all landings. Idle is the sum of positive gaps between merged intervals (start = earliest invocation start, end = outcome.at or the last invocation end). Failed minutes are the spans of jobs closed in a non-Landed state (is_failure or plan-stopped). Add `text()` with one line each for the per-day counts, the total and stage medians, idle, and failed time. Add the field to `StatusView`, set it in `Athena::status`, and write the exact-number test.

hestia.rs pure parts: constants WORSEN_RATIO=1.2, THROUGHPUT_MARKER='Throughput design: ', the priority thresholds; `throughput_due`; `priority_for_minutes`; `throughput_followups(records, current)`; and `throughput_request(proposal, review_id, section, priority)`, built with StewardRequest::new (title with the marker, a body naming the bottleneck, change and predicted saving, and a line telling authors to cite the review id, acceptance of a design note under docs/design/ with no code changes, files docs/design/).

Load Records, compute Throughput, write throughput.md and a copy of docs/design/*.md into a scratch workspace job dir (Cleanup guard, as the auditor does), then call agent_spec(Role::Steward, models.verifier, Side::Read, read-only grant) and invoke_and_record. Redact the model's words, parse and validate, apply duplicate suppression, queue through `self.queue`, then commit the ThroughputReview record (with followups) and the invocation record in one commit with Athena-Record trailers. A failure produces a record with no proposal.

risks.risk: A model call inside `review_passes` might fire in existing drain or sweep tests that script the fake driver, breaking them.
risks.mitigation: The call runs only when `throughput_due` is true, which needs at least 10 landed request jobs. Run the full cargo test; if a fixture reaches 10 landings, give it a prior review record.

risks.risk: Model failure or a malformed answer retries and spends money on every drain.
risks.mitigation: A review record with no proposal and a note is committed on any failure, which advances the cadence. The invocation record is always committed.

risks.risk: Median over a small window is noisy and may trigger 'worsened' spuriously.
risks.mitigation: The window is 20 landed jobs, the trigger needs at least one new landing, and the new review stores the current median as the next baseline, so it cannot re-trigger on the same data.

risks.risk: A crash between queuing the request and committing the review record leaves an open request with no record.
risks.mitigation: Duplicate suppression looks at the open request's marker line, not the record, so no second request is queued. The follow-up needs the record, so that review would not be followed up, which is acceptable and noted.

risks.risk: Body text of the model or the request could contain lines that start like bullets, which StewardRequest::new refuses.
risks.mitigation: Flatten the model's text with `one_line` before it enters the body. If the builder still errors, the review records the proposal without a request and a note instead of failing.

risks.risk: Adding a StatusView field or AnyRecord variant breaks exhaustive matches elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: Grep showed AnyRecord::CodeHealthBaseline handled only in records.rs, store.rs and code_health.rs, and StatusView built only in status.rs. cargo clippy --all-targets finds any other match.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in status.rs. Build an in-memory `Records` (JobRecords fields are pub) with fixed fixtures: 3 landed jobs on two UTC days with Reader/Planner/Critic/Producer/Verifier invocations of known started_at/ended_at, verification checks with known durations, and outcome.at at known offsets. Add one Rejected job with known invocations, one plan-stopped job, and gaps between job intervals. Call `Throughput::compute(&records)` (no seam is needed; it is pure and added by step 2), then assert `text()`.
demonstrations.observes: Exact numbers: landed per day (e.g. 2 and 1), median total minutes, medians for reading, planning, producer, checks, verifier and landing/rebuild, the idle minutes between jobs (overlapping jobs give 0), and the minutes on non-landed jobs. The same numbers appear in the `text()` that display.rs prints.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the computation, `Throughput::compute` does not exist and the test does not compile. If a stage were mis-attributed (planner counted as producer), the exact per-stage assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Test in hestia.rs using the existing `athena_in` temp-repo helper, changed to take a driver. It is called with `FakeAgentDriver::new(script)`, where the script returns `FakeTurn::output(json!({bottleneck, stage, change, expected_minutes_saved, rationale}))` and counts calls. Seed 10 landed jobs with `put`. Production entry point: `Athena::throughput_review(&TestUi)`. Guards: not nested, and `throughput_due` is true. The fake driver seam exists today (hestia.rs athena_in uses `FakeAgentDriver::deterministic()`; `FakeAgentDriver::new` is used in run/mod.rs and test_support.rs). Run the review twice.
demonstrations.observes: After the first run, exactly one request job is open whose text has the marker line, the bottleneck, the proposed change and the predicted minutes. One throughput-review record carries the proposal and the request job id. After the second run (forced due by 10 more landed jobs) no second request exists, a review record with `request_job: None` and a note is written, and the model was called once per review.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without duplicate suppression, the second run queues a second request and the open-request count assertion fails. Without the request builder call, no request exists.

demonstrations.method: Table test of the pure `throughput_due(landed_count, window_median, latest_review)`, called with constructed review records. Cases: no prior review with 9 landed gives None; with 10 gives Cadence; a prior review at 10 landings with 19 landed and an equal median gives None; with 20 landed gives Cadence; a prior median of 10.0 with a current median of 12.0 gives None because 20% is not more than 20%; 12.1 with at least one new landing gives Worsened; 12.1 with no new landing gives None; an improved median gives None. A second test goes through `Athena::throughput_review` with a counting fake driver: nothing is queued and the model is not called when not due, and it is called when due.
demonstrations.observes: Trigger decisions at the exact boundaries (10 landings, more than 20% worse), and zero model calls when not due.
demonstrations.fails_without: A cadence of 9 or 11, a >= comparison on 20%, or firing on every drain would each fail a boundary assertion or the call-count assertion.

demonstrations.method: Test in hestia.rs. Commit a first review record (median 20.0, a proposal with predicted saving 6.0, request_job J, id R) with `put`. Then commit a landed request job C whose text contains R, with a landing time later than the review, and 3 later landed jobs with known shorter spans. Run `Athena::throughput_review` with the fake driver, past the 10-landing mark. Also test the pure `throughput_followups(records)`.
demonstrations.observes: The new review record's `followups` holds one entry for R with predicted 6.0, baseline 20.0, the measured window median of the jobs landed after C (e.g. 15.0) and measured saving 5.0. A third review adds no second follow-up for R. A review whose cited change has not landed records none. The design request J itself, once landed, is not treated as the cited change.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the follow-up step, `followups` is empty and the assertion on predicted against measured fails.

demonstrations.method: Test the pure `priority_for_minutes` with 0.5, 2.0, 5.0 and 10.0, 25.0, and assert the mapping low, normal, high, urgent, urgent. In the fake-model review test, run two repositories with predicted savings of 12.0 and 1.0 and assert the queued request text starts `Priority: urgent` and `Priority: low`. Assert the order is non-decreasing across an increasing series. Entry point: `Athena::throughput_review`, the seam as in criterion 2.
demonstrations.observes: The queued requests' Priority lines and `Records::priority()` of the queued jobs rise with the saving.
demonstrations.fails_without: A constant priority makes the 12.0 and 1.0 requests carry the same level and the assertion fails.
